investigation.title: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Remote Agent Checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents feature checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-09-02T22:03–22:04Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm gateway ELB endpoint was unreachable during agent provisioning. Because the failure occurs at POST /api/agents before any agent identity or VM state is returned, all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is absent and every contract assertion is unverifiable.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — the AWS ELB-backed service at the redacted us-east-2 endpoint that handles POST /v1/agents — was unreachable at the time of the eval run. The production-api layer returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" on every attempt to provision a remote agent, preventing the runner from obtaining any agent identity or VM state. This is an infrastructure-layer failure localized to the swarm gateway dependency, not to the eval runner logic or the expected-output contract definitions. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is confirmed only at the eval layer.

The error message references an HTTP-level send failure ('error sending request for url'), which is consistent with a TCP-level or DNS-level connectivity break rather than an application error.

Lower probability — The eval runner's access token or org credentials were rejected upstream, but this is unlikely because the error code is bad_gateway (502) rather than unauthorized (401/403), and the runner did not return the SKIP status that would indicate a missing token (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1882).
